package_info.package_name: Inventa (third-party supplier script used on Ticketmaster)
package_info.package_manager: Web (JavaScript injected via third-party web plugin)
package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions in use during the Magecart attack)
package_info.why_malicious: The Inventa third-party web script was compromised and injected with Magecart card-skimming malware, which harvested sensitive payment card data from users entering information on Ticketmaster’s online forms and exfiltrated it to a remote command and control server. This behavior is malicious because it covertly steals user credentials and payment data without consent.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user interacts with payment/login forms)
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript within third-party web plugin (Inventa) loaded on Ticketmaster payment pages

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the payment form's submit event, collects sensitive card data from input fields, and sends this data via HTTPS POST to a remote command and control server, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting form submissions and exfiltrating sensitive data to an external server is a classic sign of credential harvesting malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal third-party scripts should not access or transmit payment credentials to external domains; legitimate analytics or support scripts do not require raw card data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form validation scripts may access form fields, but should not transmit sensitive data offsite except to trusted payment processors.
key_indicators: Access to payment or login form fields
Network requests to untrusted or external domains

attack_chain.action: Magecart group compromises the Inventa third-party script and injects malicious JavaScript skimmer code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded on Ticketmaster payment pages.

attack_chain.action: When a user enters payment data and submits the form, the malicious script intercepts the data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive card data is captured in the browser.

attack_chain.action: The script sends the harvested card data to a remote command and control server controlled by the attackers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attackers receive stolen credentials for further exploitation or sale.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code hooking into payment or login form submission events
Collection of sensitive input field values (e.g., card number, CVV, password)
Outbound network requests to domains not associated with the legitimate service
Exfiltration of form data at runtime
file_indicators: Unexpected changes or additions to third-party web scripts
Injected or obfuscated JavaScript within vendor-supplied plugins
Scripts loaded from domains not previously used by the site
network_indicators: POST requests from client browsers to unknown or suspicious external domains (e.g., not Ticketmaster or payment processor)
Unusual traffic patterns from payment pages to new endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript code on payment or login pages that accesses sensitive form fields and initiates network requests to untrusted domains. Use content security policy (CSP) to restrict script sources and outbound connections. Regularly audit third-party scripts for unauthorized modifications or suspicious behaviors, and inspect network logs for exfiltration attempts from client-side code.
